```python
def parse_slide_timeline(
    slide_xml: bytes,
    slide_key: str,
    targets: Mapping[int, ResolvedTarget],

```
`targets` maps an OOXML shape id (p:spTgt/@spid) to the already-resolved ResolvedTarget (another module owns building it). An effect whose spid is missing from `targets` is NOT a crash and NOT silently dropped: record it as UnsupportedEffect(reason_code="unresolved_target", ...).

VERIFIED OOXML FACTS (I probed real files this session — trust these, do not re-derive):
- Namespaces: p = http://schemas.openxmlformats.org/presentationml/2006/main, a = http://schemas.openxmlformats.org/drawingml/2006/main.
- Slide-level shape ids live on `p:cNvPr` (PRESENTATION namespace in slide XML, NOT a:cNvPr — this trips people up).
- lxml's `.find()` does NOT support the `local-name()` XPath function; use `.xpath(".//*[local-name()='spTgt']")` when you need namespace-agnostic lookup, or fully-qualified `{ns}tag` with .find/.findall.
- Timeline structure: `p:timing/p:tnLst/p:par/p:cTn[@nodeType='tmRoot']/p:childTnLst/p:seq[p:cTn/@nodeType='mainSeq']`. The click groups are `seq/p:cTn/p:childTnLst/p:par` — they are NOT direct children of p:seq. Each such par nests par/cTn wrappers about three levels deep before the effect cTn.
- The effect cTn is the descendant cTn carrying `presetID` (also `presetClass`, `presetSubtype`, `grpId`, `nodeType` in {clickEffect, withEffect, afterEffect}).
- Behavior elements found under the effect cTn: `p:animEffect` (attrs transition=in|out, filter="fade"/"wipe(left)"/... ), `p:anim` (attrs clrSpc, dir, from, to — color changes), `p:animMotion` (attrs origin, path like "M 0 1 L 0 0 L 0 0 E", pathEditMode, ptsTypes), `p:set`, `p:animScale`, `p:animRot`, `p:animClr`.
- Duration: `behavior/p:cBhvr/p:cTn/@dur` in milliseconds (may be "indefinite").
- Delay: the effect cTn's `p:stCondLst/p:cond/@delay` (may be "indefinite" for the click wait — that means 0 delay once triggered).
- Target: `behavior/p:cBhvr/p:tgtEl/p:spTgt/@spid`. A `p:txtEl`/`p:txtTgtEl` under tgtEl means the effect targets a text range rather than the whole shape.
- Slide transition: `p:sld/p:transition` with attrs (spid, advClick, advTm) and exactly one child element naming the kind (e.g. `p:fade`, `p:push`, `p:wipe`).
- Working reference dump from a real deck I parsed: effect 1 = presetID 1 / presetClass entr / animEffect(transition=in, filter=fade) / dur 500 / spid 2; effect 2 = presetID 2 / presetClass entr / animMotion(path="M 0 1 L 0 0 L 0 0 E") / dur 1000 / spid 3; effect 3 = presetID 11 / presetClass emph / anim(clrSpc=rgb, from=#0070C0, to=#FF0000) / dur 300 / spid 2.

MAPPING RULES (fail-closed — this is the whole point):
- presetClass entr -> EffectClass.ENTRANCE, exit -> EXIT, emph -> EMPHASIS, path -> MOTION. Any other presetClass -> UnsupportedEffect(reason_code="unknown_preset_class").
- nodeType clickEffect -> EffectTrigger.ON_CLICK, withEffect -> WITH_PREVIOUS, afterEffect -> AFTER_PREVIOUS. Anything else -> UnsupportedEffect(reason_code="unknown_trigger").
- Behavior -> contract behavior: animEffect filter starting with "fade" -> FadeBehavior(direction from @transition); filter starting with "wipe" -> WipeBehavior (parse the edge from forms like "wipe(left)"/"wipe(up)"; PowerPoint's wipe direction words are left/right/up/down); animMotion -> MotionBehavior(path=@path, cleaned to the safe charset the contract enforces); anim with clrSpc/from/to hex colors -> ColorBehavior. EVERYTHING ELSE (set, animScale, animRot, unknown filters, malformed colors, missing dur) -> UnsupportedEffect with a precise reason_code and detail. NEVER approximate an effect you cannot map exactly — a wrong animation on stage is worse than a refused one.
- Text-range targets (txtEl/txtTgtEl present) -> UnsupportedEffect(reason_code="text_range_target") in this increment; record, never drop.
- Durations: "indefinite" or missing -> UnsupportedEffect(reason_code="indefinite_duration") EXCEPT when the behavior is otherwise valid and the deck simply used the default; if @dur is absent entirely, treat as 0 only when a p:cTn sibling supplies it, otherwise unsupported. Clamp to the contract's 0..600000 range; out-of-range -> unsupported.
- Click groups: preserve document order. Group N contains the clickEffect that starts it plus the withEffect/afterEffect effects nested in that same top-level par.
- Deterministic output: same input bytes -> identical SlideTimeline every time.

TDD IS MANDATORY: write the failing test first, run it, confirm the failure reason, then implement. Build test decks with python-pptx and inject p:timing XML via lxml (python-pptx has no animation API — construct `<p:timing>` yourself and append it to `slide._element`; a `<p:transition>` element likewise; remember to substitute real shape ids from `shape.shape_id`).
